applies_why: The judge text counts Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 toward a broken link by saying they contradict C3, without quoting an earlier-round pressing sentence or naming that round.
quote: D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way.
room: The phrase 'A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way': either the verses the judge lists as contradicting C3 count toward the broken link, or they do not because no explicit counting wording appears; I weighed those.
why: The judge declares the challenger link broken using Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 but names no earlier round and quotes no earlier-round pressing sentence, so it counts verses toward a broken link contrary to K-G4.
